Those who do not know demand that Allah speak to them or send a sign, but the Prophet is sent with the truth to give good tidings and warn.
Allah sent a messenger from among them to recite His verses, purify them and teach them the Book and wisdom, so remember Him and be grateful.
Muhammad is only a messenger like those before him; if he died or were killed, turning back would not harm Allah, who rewards the grateful.
By Allah's mercy the Prophet was lenient with them; he is told to pardon them, seek forgiveness for them, consult them, then rely on Allah.
Allah favored the believers by sending a Messenger from among them to recite His verses, purify them and teach them the Book and wisdom.
By Allah's favor and mercy a group failed to mislead the Prophet; Allah revealed to him the Book and wisdom and taught him what he did not know.
The Messenger is told to convey what was revealed to him, or he has not delivered Allah's message, and Allah will protect him from the people.
They reject Allah's verses, not the Prophet; earlier messengers bore denial patiently, had Allah willed He would have united them on guidance, and only those who hear respond.
The Prophet says he holds no depositories of Allah, does not know the unseen and is not an angel; he only follows what is revealed to him.
The Prophet declares he is forbidden to worship what they invoke, stands on clear evidence from his Lord, and does not hold what they impatiently demand; the decision is Allah's.
The Prophet is told to follow what is revealed to him and turn from those who associate others with Allah, for he is not their guardian or manager.
Those who follow the unlettered prophet, written of in the Torah and Gospel, will succeed; he declares he is Allah's Messenger to all mankind, to be believed and followed.
The Prophet holds no power to benefit or harm himself except as Allah wills, does not know the unseen, and is only a warner and bringer of good tidings.
The disbelievers plotted to restrain, kill or evict the Prophet, but Allah also plans, and He is the best of planners.
A Messenger has come from among them, grieved by their suffering, kind and merciful to believers; if they turn away, he relies on Allah, Lord of the Great Throne.
The disbelievers say he is not a messenger; he answers that Allah, and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture, is sufficient witness between them.
They nearly tempted the Prophet away from the revelation, but Allah strengthened him; they nearly drove him out, yet as with earlier messengers, they would not remain long after.
The Prophet is told he might destroy himself with grief over those who do not believe in this message.
The Prophet, sent as a mercy to the worlds, announces your god is one God, does not know when the promise comes, and asks his Lord to judge in truth.
Whoever thinks Allah will not support the Prophet in this world and the Hereafter is told to stretch a rope to the ceiling and see if that removes his rage.
They neither reflect on the Quran nor acknowledge their Messenger, calling him mad, though he brought the truth, asks no payment and invites them to a straight path.
Believers ask the Messenger's permission before leaving a gathering, should not call him as they call each other, and those dissenting from his order should beware.
They ask why this messenger eats food and walks in markets without an angel, treasure or garden, calling him bewitched, though Allah could give him better gardens and palaces.
Allah could have sent a warner to every city but sent the Prophet to all, so he must not obey the disbelievers but strive against them with the Quran.
The Prophet is sent only to give good tidings and warn, asking no payment except that whoever wills may take a way to his Lord.
The Prophet is told to warn his closest kindred, lower his wing to believing followers, disown the disobedient's deeds, and rely on Allah who sees him among those who prostrate.
The Prophet is commanded to worship the Lord of this sacred city, be a Muslim and recite the Quran; the guided benefit themselves, and Allah will show His signs.
The Prophet was not present when Moses received the command, nor in Madyan, but is sent as a mercy to warn a people who had no warner before him.
He who imposed the Quran will return the Prophet to a place of return; the Book is a mercy, so he must not aid disbelievers but invite to his Lord.
The Prophet is told to fear Allah, not obey the disbelievers and hypocrites, follow what is revealed to him, and rely on Allah.
The Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves and his wives are their mothers, while blood relatives are more entitled to inherit than other believers and emigrants.
The Messenger of Allah is an excellent example for anyone hoping in Allah and the Last Day and remembering Allah often.
The Prophet's wives are to choose worldly adornment or Allah and the Hereafter, face double punishment or reward, speak properly, stay in their houses, pray, give zakah and obey.
Once Zayd no longer needed his wife Zaynab, Allah married her to the Prophet, removing believers' discomfort over adopted sons' wives; Muhammad is Allah's Messenger and last of the prophets.
The Prophet is sent as witness, bringer of good tidings, warner, caller to Allah and illuminating lamp, told not to obey disbelievers and hypocrites but to rely on Allah.
Allah sets out the women lawful for the Prophet, lets him choose among his wives, then forbids him more wives or exchanges, except those his right hand possesses.
Allah blesses the Prophet and His angels ask for it, and believers are told to ask Allah to bless him and grant him peace.
The Prophet is sent to all mankind as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, though most people do not know.
The Prophet urges people to stand for Allah in pairs or singly and reflect: he is no madman but a warner, asking no payment and guided by revelation.
By the wise Quran, the Prophet is among the messengers on a straight path, with revelation from the Exalted, the Merciful, to warn a people whose forefathers were not warned.
The Prophet says he is only a clear warner, that there is no deity but Allah, the One, and that he had no knowledge of the exalted assembly's dispute.
Some say the Prophet invented a lie about Allah, but Allah could seal his heart if He willed, and He erases falsehood and establishes truth by His words.
The Prophet cannot make the deaf hear; Allah will take retribution whether or not he sees it, so he holds to the revelation, a reminder for him and his people.
The Prophet's saying that these people do not believe is acknowledged; he is told to turn aside from them and say 'Peace', for they will come to know.
The Prophet is sent as a witness, bringer of good tidings and warner, so people believe in Allah and His Messenger, honor him and exalt Allah morning and afternoon.
Allah sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, and Allah is sufficient as Witness.
The Prophet, no soothsayer or madman, is told to keep reminding; to those who call him a poet and await his misfortune, he says, 'Wait,' for he waits with them.
By the star, the Prophet has not strayed; his words are revelation taught by Gabriel, intense in strength, whom he saw near and again at the Lote Tree.
Allah, whom all creation exalts, sent the unlettered a Messenger from among them to recite His verses, purify them and teach them the Book and wisdom, a bounty from Allah.
The Prophet forbade himself the lawful to please his wives; after a wife disclosed his secret, two are urged to repent, and all told he could have better wives.
By the pen, the Prophet is not mad by his Lord's favor; he has an unending reward and a great moral character, and his Lord knows who has strayed.
Disbelievers nearly make the Prophet slip with their eyes when they hear the message and call him mad, but it is only a reminder to the worlds.
The Prophet says he invokes only his Lord, has no power to harm or guide them, finds no refuge but Allah and only conveys His messages; disobeyers face Hell.
The one covered in a garment is told to arise and warn, glorify his Lord, purify his clothing, avoid uncleanliness, not give to gain more, and be patient.
The Prophet frowned and turned from a blind man, Ibn Umm Maktum, who came seeking purification, while attending to one who thought himself without need.
The Prophet is only a reminder, not a controller; Allah will punish whoever turns away and disbelieves, for their return and account are with Him.
Allah has not left the Prophet; He sheltered him as an orphan, guided and enriched him, so he must not oppress orphans or repel petitioners, and must report His favor.
Allah expanded the Prophet's breast, lifted his burden and raised his repute; with hardship comes ease, so after finishing, stand up in worship and long for your Lord.
Allah granted the Prophet al-Kawthar, so he should pray to his Lord and sacrifice, and his enemy is the one cut off.
